title: Shannon-Hartley limit
references: Shannon, C. E., A Mathematical Theory of Communication, Bell System Technical Journal 27(3), 379-423 (1948), doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x
Cover, T. M. and Thomas, J. A., Elements of Information Theory, 2nd ed., Wiley (2006)
validity_domain: Error-free information rate over a band-limited channel of bandwidth B with additive white Gaussian noise and a signal-to-noise power ratio snr (a plain ratio, not decibels).
limitations: Additive white Gaussian noise channel; other noise or fading channels have other capacities
snr is the linear power ratio over the bandwidth B; a value in dB must be converted first
Capacity of the channel, reached only with ideal coding: a link does not reach it
Defined for a positive bandwidth and a non-negative ratio snr; the core checks no condition on them here
Multiple antennas or users (MIMO) are not covered
